content.comment_body: Hello, I have attempted communication between [product_name] and [version_no], but I am currently unable to correctly read the scaled analog value from [version_no] into [product_name]. Is there a sample program or example available for achieving this? Thank you.

[product_name] is only capable of processing integer values and does not support floating point numbers. If you encounter a floating point value, it must be converted to integer format. Ensure the number remains within the range of 32767 to -32768. For example: 127.65 multiplied by 100 becomes 12765, which is then stored as an integer. Send this value to [product_name]; you can use arithmetic operations or other instructions to display it with two decimal places.
Thank you for the prompt reply. That information is very helpful.

Hello, I have already performed the multiplication of the scaled analog value on the [product_name] software side. I am now receiving the value from [version_no] in [product_name]. For instance, if the analog value at the [product_name] software side is 0.144, it appears as 144 in [product_name]. I am unsure how to convert it back for display with the decimal point using arithmetic operations or similar methods. Is there a sample or guidance available for this? Any assistance is appreciated. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge users face is integrating [product_name] and [version_no] controllers to properly acquire and display analog input values. Since [product_name] does not support floating point numbers, values must be converted to integers and then formatted for display. Users are seeking sample programs or instructions to manage conversion and display of these values with accurate decimal representation.

They also request sample programs or clear step-by-step instructions to facilitate proper data handling in this scenario.
